nodes.label: Ancient Oikonomia
nodes.note: Economy as stewardship of the household for the good life — embedded in ethics

nodes.label: Scholastic Economics
nodes.sub: Aquinas, Oresme · just price, usury ban
nodes.note: Economic activity subordinated to moral law — the price should be just, not merely market

nodes.label: Islamic Economics
nodes.note: Asabiyyah (social cohesion) as economic foundation — wealth serves community bonds

nodes.label: Commons / Guilds
nodes.note: Economic life embedded in community — production as participation, not extraction

nodes.label: Mercantilism
nodes.note: THE FORK — economy redefined as national power; wealth as zero-sum conquest

nodes.label: Adam Smith
nodes.note: Genuinely both — moral philosopher first; invisible hand within moral sentiments

nodes.label: Physiocrats
nodes.note: Nature as source of value — still participatory, but beginning to model & abstract

nodes.label: Ricardo / Classical
nodes.sub: Comparative advantage, iron law of wages
nodes.note: Ethics recedes — laws of economics as impersonal mechanism, like Newtonian physics

nodes.label: Marx
nodes.note: Diagnosed alienation (loss of participation) but prescribed another instrumentalism

nodes.label: Marginalist Revolution
nodes.note: Value = subjective utility; economics becomes calculus; the human becomes a function

nodes.label: Institutional Economics
nodes.note: Economy is embedded in society, not the other way around — recovered participation

nodes.label: Keynesian
nodes.note: Government manages aggregate demand — technocratic but acknowledges human irrationality

nodes.label: Austrian School
nodes.note: Distributed knowledge, anti-planning — genuinely anti-instrumentalist epistemology

nodes.label: Welfare State
nodes.note: Economy serves human needs — partial recovery of oikonomia through redistribution

nodes.label: Chicago School
nodes.note: Everything is a market — marriage, crime, children all modeled as utility optimization

nodes.label: Neoclassical Synthesis
nodes.note: Elegant math, fictional humans — representative agents maximizing in perfect markets

nodes.label: Ecological Economics
nodes.note: Economy as subsystem of biosphere — nature has intrinsic value, not just resource value

nodes.label: Behavioral Economics
nodes.note: Humans aren't rational — but the fix is to manipulate their irrationality more cleverly

nodes.label: Financialization
nodes.note: Money making money — value abstracted from all human good; chrematistike triumphant

nodes.label: Commons Revival
nodes.note: Communities CAN manage shared resources — neither state nor market needed

nodes.label: Degrowth / Doughnut
nodes.note: Correct diagnosis, naive politics — vulnerable to capture by the power it critiques

nodes.label: Local / Solidarity Economy
nodes.note: Economic life re-embedded in community — participation over extraction

nodes.label: Stakeholder Capitalism
nodes.note: Acknowledges the problem, instrumentalizes the solution — greenwashing risk

nodes.label: Algorithmic Trading
nodes.note: Machines trading with machines — humans fully removed from economic activity

nodes.label: Platform Capitalism
nodes.note: Extract value from human activity without employing humans — digital enclosure

nodes.label: Crypto / DeFi
nodes.note: Decentralized but not re-embedded — speculation without community

nodes.label: Sovereign Debt / MMT-as-weapon
nodes.note: Entire nations as debt-servicing entities — economy consumes the polity

title: The Triumph of Chrematistike
description: Aristotle distinguished oikonomia (household management for flourishing) from chrematistike (money-making as its own end). Every node on this chart is a position in that ancient argument. Hover for diagnostic notes.

explanatoryNote.heading: Aristotle named it 2,400 years ago:
explanatoryNote.text: Chrematistike — money-making as its own end — is "unnatural" because it has no inherent limit. Oikonomia aims at sufficiency for the good life; chrematistike aims at infinite accumulation. Adam Smith at 55 is the bridge — moral philosopher who also unleashed the market; Theory of Moral Sentiments and Wealth of Nations are the two halves of his Catholicism. The Marginalist Revolution at 12 is the nominalist fork — value becomes subjective utility, economics becomes calculus, the human becomes a maximizing function. The Austrian School at 38 preserves genuine anti-instrumentalist insight — distributed knowledge, anti-planning — but still treats the human as a maximizer. Degrowth at 35 correctly diagnoses infinite growth on a finite planet but has no viable theory of transition and is vulnerable to capture by power. Ostrom and the commons revival proved communities can manage shared resources without either state or market — the thin teal stream. Algorithmic trading at 1: machines trading with machines, humans fully removed. Aristotle's nightmare.
